_description: Labeled relevance corpus for the retrieval-quality harness (tests/e2e/test_retrieval_quality.rs). Unlike retrieval_corpus.json (threshold-alignment fixtures), this file is a graded relevance set: every query names the skill id(s) that are RELEVANT, so the harness can compute precision@k / recall@k / MRR / nDCG against ground truth and compare the live semantic ranking against an in-harness pure-lexical baseline. Query kinds: 'lexical' (shares literal tokens with its skill), 'disjoint' (semantically about its skill but deliberately avoids the skill's literal tokens — only real embeddings can bridge it), 'negative' (no skill is relevant; the system must NOT fabricate a match). This file is OWNED by the quality harness and is NOT the shared retrieval_corpus.json.

_thresholds.note: Honest bars. These are targets, not guarantees — the harness asserts them and is EXPECTED to fail loudly when retrieval quality regresses or under-delivers. Do not relax them to make the suite green; fix retrieval.

skills.description: Asynchronous file input and output in Rust using the tokio runtime — non-blocking reads and writes, streaming large files, and error boundaries at async IO seams.

subunits.title: Read a file without blocking
subunits.content: Use tokio::fs::read_to_string for small files; wrap large files in a tokio BufReader and stream line by line so the executor thread is never blocked on disk.

subunits.title: Never block the async executor on disk
subunits.content: Avoid std::fs in an async context; a synchronous read stalls the whole runtime thread. Prefer spawn_blocking only when no async API exists.

skills.description: Managing PostgreSQL connection pools with sqlx — sizing the pool, acquiring and releasing handles, and surviving bursts of concurrent requests without exhausting the database.

subunits.title: Size and share one pool
subunits.content: Create a single sqlx::PgPool at startup and clone it into handlers; never open a fresh connection per request. Bound max_connections to what the database can serve.

subunits.title: Release handles promptly
subunits.content: Hold an acquired connection for the shortest possible scope so a spike of simultaneous callers does not drain the available handles.

skills.description: Health gating between services in Docker Compose — defining health probes and making a dependent container wait until the service it needs is actually ready before it boots.

subunits.title: Gate startup on readiness
subunits.content: Add a HEALTHCHECK to the dependency and use depends_on condition: service_healthy so the consumer does not start until the probe passes.

subunits.title: Probe cheaply
subunits.content: Use a lightweight readiness probe (pg_isready, a TCP check) rather than a full query so the health loop stays fast.

skills.description: Resolving merge conflicts during an interactive git rebase — replaying commits one at a time, reconciling diverging histories hunk by hunk, and continuing or aborting the replay safely.

subunits.title: Reconcile each replayed commit
subunits.content: When a replayed commit collides, edit the conflicting hunks, stage the resolution, and continue the replay; abort to restore the original branch if it goes wrong.

subunits.title: Replay onto an updated base
subunits.content: Reapply your work on top of the latest upstream tip so the diverging lines of history converge into one linear sequence.

skills.description: Consuming a Redis stream with consumer groups — reading new entries, acknowledging processed messages, and recovering pending un-acked work after a crash so nothing is silently lost.

subunits.title: Read, process, then acknowledge
subunits.content: XREADGROUP to claim new entries, do the work, then XACK so the entry leaves the pending list; an entry stays pending until acknowledged.

subunits.title: Recover orphaned work after a crash
subunits.content: On restart, inspect the pending entries list and re-claim un-acknowledged messages so a mid-flight failure does not drop the event.

skills.description: Resilience for flaky downstream calls — retrying a transient failure with exponential backoff and jitter, and giving up after a bounded number of attempts instead of hammering a struggling dependency.

subunits.title: Back off between attempts
subunits.content: On a transient error, wait an exponentially growing, jittered delay before the next attempt; cap the total attempts so a dead dependency is not retried forever.

subunits.title: Only retry idempotent work
subunits.content: Retry reads and idempotent writes; never blindly re-issue a non-idempotent side effect, or a flapping call can double-apply it.

skills.description: Structured, contextual logging in Rust with the tracing crate — emitting machine-parseable key/value events and wrapping work in spans so a request can be followed across async boundaries.

subunits.title: Wrap work in a span
subunits.content: Open a tracing span around a unit of work and attach fields; child events inherit the span context so the whole operation can be reconstructed from logs.

subunits.title: Log key/value, not prose
subunits.content: Emit structured fields instead of interpolated sentences so logs are queryable and correlate across a request's lifetime.

skills.description: Ranking dense embedding vectors by cosine similarity — measuring the angle between a query vector and candidate vectors to order them by semantic closeness rather than literal word overlap.

subunits.title: Score by the angle between vectors
subunits.content: Normalize both vectors and take their dot product; the closer the cosine is to 1 the more semantically aligned the candidate is with the query.

subunits.title: Closeness is meaning, not spelling
subunits.content: Two passages with no shared words can still score high if their embeddings point the same way — rank by meaning, not token overlap.
